label: Agriculture
description: Crop science, farm practices, water, climate, and agricultural markets.

suggested_queries.label: Yellowing tomatoes
suggested_queries.query: A small rain-fed tomato plot sits in heavy clay. After two weeks of wet weather, lower leaves are yellowing. I have not measured soil moisture or pH, and I have not confirmed pests. Compare drainage, nutrient, and pest explanations using only these facts. Give me three low-risk observations to make before changing inputs, and say what location or field evidence is needed before recommending a treatment.

suggested_queries.label: Check irrigation first
suggested_queries.query: I want a drip schedule for a vegetable bed, but I only know the crop and approximate bed size. What measurements are essential before suggesting a schedule? Separate measurements I can take now from assumptions that would make a schedule unreliable.

suggested_queries.label: Scout before treating
suggested_queries.query: I see new chewing damage on leaves but have not found an insect. Give me a short scouting sequence that could distinguish pest damage from weather or mechanical damage. Say what evidence would justify treatment and what local information is still needed; do not invent a pesticide rate or label direction.

label: Software
description: Simple software design, implementation, testing, security, and accessibility.

suggested_queries.label: Resume one failed call
suggested_queries.query: In a single-user FastAPI tool, I want to save a partially completed roundtable and resume only the failed call. The existing database can store successful answers, but I have not shared the route or storage code. Propose the smallest useful change, the state that must be saved, and acceptance checks proving successful answers are not repeated. Identify what you cannot determine without seeing the code.

suggested_queries.label: Keep the form recoverable
suggested_queries.query: A provider timeout currently replaces a submitted form with an error. Design the smallest change that keeps the question and completed answers visible while offering a retry. Cover keyboard access, status feedback, and the failure case where retry also fails.

suggested_queries.label: Review exported data
suggested_queries.query: A local advisor tool exports prompts and AI responses as Markdown. Map what could be exposed in the prompt, export, and saved history. Separate facts from assumptions, and list the settings or code that must be checked before claiming the data is private.

label: AI Workflow & Delegation
description: Decide what to delegate to AI, what context to provide, and how to review and recover.

suggested_queries.label: Delegate release notes
suggested_queries.query: I want a remote AI coding agent to draft release notes from a diff I supply. It may read that diff and write one draft to an approved scratch location, but it cannot edit the repository or commit, push, merge, or publish. Give me the actual compact task packet, not advice to create one. Include three checks that trace each material claim to a changed hunk; mark them pending if no diff is present. Add a resume checkpoint with the input reference or hash only if available, exact instructions, draft location, status, and next step. Compare total human setup, review, correction, and recovery time with similar manual drafting; do not claim savings without a measured baseline. Distinguish prompt rules from enforceable tool permissions, and require approval or redaction before sending the diff to the hosted model.

suggested_queries.label: Bound a code change
suggested_queries.query: I want an AI agent to update one settings page in a local app. It may edit that page and its focused styles, but must not change authentication, data storage, or publish the app. Define the inputs, one reviewable deliverable, the acceptance check, and the exact stop condition if it discovers a wider dependency.

suggested_queries.label: Resume after interruption
suggested_queries.query: I often stop work mid-task and return without the full conversation. Design a tiny handoff record for an AI coding task: what is done, current files, next action, open decision, and recovery command. Keep it short enough to dictate and say what should never be inferred from the note.

suggested_queries.label: Bound a handoff
suggested_queries.query: Draft a handoff for one bounded task. Task: [name]. Allowed: [inputs it may read and where it may write]. Blocked: [edits, commits, publishing]. Deliverable: [one reviewable draft]. Today's change: [diff or input supplied].

label: Accessibility & Effort
description: Reduce input, handoffs, and effort across everyday tasks, with accessible ways to resume.

suggested_queries.label: Reduce repeated dictation
suggested_queries.query: I use dictation and short work sessions. A recurring task currently means re-entering the same background and remembering several steps. Redesign it around one reusable, voice-friendly starter, the fewest practical interactions, and a saved checkpoint I can resume after an interruption. Ask at most one essential question. Include a fallback if dictation fails and keep the final choice with me.

suggested_queries.label: Make status easy to hear
suggested_queries.query: A long-running task can take several minutes and sometimes fails. Propose concise spoken and on-screen status messages for started, waiting, completed, and failed states. Make it clear what is saved and what action is available, without requiring the person to reread a long transcript.

suggested_queries.label: Find the smallest effort cut
suggested_queries.query: A form requires repeating the same information across three steps. Suggest the smallest safe reduction in input. State what must persist if the person pauses, how they can correct an accidental selection, and what to test with keyboard and assistive technology.

suggested_queries.label: Shrink repeated input
suggested_queries.query: Reduce repeated input for one recurring task. Task: [name]. Background ref: [link or None]. Goal: [one outcome]. Next: [one action]. Give a reusable starter, an exact resume checkpoint, a dictation fallback, and one small trial. Today's change: [what differs today].

label: Evidence & Judgment
description: Examine claims, source quality, competing explanations, and uncertainty in supplied material.

suggested_queries.label: Test the 50% claim
suggested_queries.query: A small AI coding pilot is said to cut review effort by 50% because its changes received fewer review comments. There is no human-only baseline, review time was not tracked, and the changes varied in size. Separate what the evidence supports from what it does not. Give one plausible alternative explanation and the smallest fair measurement that could change the conclusion. Do not treat agreement among AI advisors as evidence.

suggested_queries.label: Compare explanations
suggested_queries.query: Two explanations fit the same short report. I will paste the report and both explanations. Identify which statements are directly supported, what each explanation assumes, one observation that would distinguish them, and what result would change your current view. Do not force a winner if the supplied evidence cannot decide.

suggested_queries.label: Check a source-backed answer
suggested_queries.query: I will paste an answer and its cited passages. Match each consequential claim to the passage that supports it, flag unsupported leaps or missing dates, and list the smallest source check that could change the conclusion. Do not claim to open or verify links I have not supplied as text.

suggested_queries.label: Test one claim
suggested_queries.query: Test one claim before I act on it. Claim: [paste claim]. Decision it blocks: [decision]. Supplied evidence (optional): Source label: [label or not supplied]. Passage: [paste relevant text or not supplied]. Treat a URL or file path as a reference, not contents you can open. Separate supplied facts from inference, leave missing evidence unknown, and give the smallest check that could change the conclusion. Today's change: [what is new].
